title: Annotatio IV §.XVI close: Transubstantiation in spiritual sense — exhibitivum in worthy mouth — stop before §.XVII
pass_a_gloss: even the monstrous vocabulary of Transubstantiation, Rainerius witnessing, they by no means flee — yet in a Spiritual sense — when they teach that Transubstantiation does not happen in the hand of the one confecting but in the mouth of the one worthily taking: Not as if they thought bread in the mouth of the worthily taking is converted into the substance of Christ’s body, but that they judged the Sacrament also in its own mode in the mouth of the worthily taking to be not only significative (as also in the mouth of the impious) but also exhibitive of the Lord’s body and blood, inasmuch as, the symbols taken by the faithful’s bodily mouth, at the same time also the thing signified — the body and blood of Christ — is perceived by the taste of faith.
pass_b_english: They do not flee the word Transubstantiation (Rainerius) — but take it spiritually: not in the consecrator’s hand, but in the worthy receiver’s mouth.

Not bread converted into substance there, but the Sacrament exhibitive (not only significative) of the Lord’s body and blood — symbols in the body’s mouth, the thing signified perceived by faith’s taste. Stop before §.XVII.
source_text: etiam Transsubstantiationis portentosum vocabulum, teste Rainerio, sensu tamen Spirituali, haud defugientes, quando docent, Transsubstantiationem non fieri in manu conficientis, sed in ore dignè sumentis: Non, quasi panem in ore dignè sumentium in substantiam corporis Christi converti putassent, sed quod Sacramentum arbitrati sint etiam suo modo in ore dignè sumentium non tantum significativum (quale & in ore impiorum) sed & exhibitivum corporis & sanguinis Domini esse, quatenus sumtis, ore corporis fidelium, symbolis, simul & res significata, corpus & sanguis Christi, gustu fidei percipiuntur.

lemmas.latin: non … in manu conficientis, sed in ore
lemmas.gloss: not in the confecting hand but in the mouth
